answer: Paired-shard issuance. Each identity draws a grove of two shards that must act jointly on any coordination request; single-shard actions are rejected. To create a second identity, an attacker must acquire an independently issued shard pair and encrypt each transaction under a distinct cipher key, so costs multiply per clone rather than plateau. Every approved action emits a ripple of counterparty acknowledgments that must settle within one epoch, forcing attackers to sustain live bidirectionally on every shard simultaneously.
